passages.title: Electric Motorbikes: Time to Switch?
text: Electric motorbikes are becoming a common sight on Indonesian roads, partly because the government has offered subsidies to make them cheaper. Yet many riders are still unsure whether they should replace their petrol motorbikes. The debate involves cost, convenience, and the environment.

Supporters point out that electric motorbikes are much cheaper to run. Charging a battery at home costs only a fraction of the price of filling a tank with petrol, and since an electric motor has far fewer moving parts, maintenance is simpler and less frequent. They also argue that electric motorbikes reduce air pollution in cities, because they produce no exhaust while being ridden.

Critics, on the other hand, highlight several practical problems. Public charging stations are still rare outside big cities, and a full charge may take several hours. Most models can travel only around sixty to a hundred kilometres before they need recharging, which is a serious limitation for delivery riders who travel long distances every day. Some critics also question the environmental benefit, noting that much of Indonesia's electricity is still generated by burning coal.

Batteries are another concern. They are expensive to replace and must be recycled properly; otherwise, the chemicals inside can harm soil and water. Nevertheless, battery-swapping stations, where riders exchange an empty battery for a full one in a few minutes, are starting to appear in several cities and may solve the charging problem.

On balance, electric motorbikes appear to be a sensible choice for riders who travel short distances in cities with good charging facilities. For others, it may be wiser to wait until the infrastructure improves and more electricity comes from clean sources.

passages.title: Your Data, Your Responsibility
text: Every time we sign up for an app, join a contest, or fill in an online form, we hand over pieces of personal information: our names, birth dates, phone numbers, and sometimes even photos of our identity cards. Most of us do this without a second thought. This carelessness is dangerous, and it is time we took our own data privacy seriously.

The most obvious risk is fraud. Criminals who obtain a person's identity card number and phone number can use them to register for online loans or to take over social media accounts. In recent years, police in several countries have reported a sharp rise in such cases, many of which began with data that victims had shared freely.

Moreover, personal data has become a valuable product. Many free apps earn money by collecting information about users' habits and selling it to advertisers. While targeted advertising may seem harmless, the same information can be used to influence people's choices, from what they buy to which political messages they see.

Admittedly, governments and companies also have a responsibility to protect data, and laws such as Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law, passed in 2022, are an important step. However, laws cannot protect people who give their data away carelessly. Data leaks also happen even in large organizations, so the less we share, the less can be stolen.

Protecting our privacy does not require advanced technical skills. Reading an app's permissions before installing it, refusing to send photos of identity documents to unknown parties, and using different passwords for different accounts are simple habits that make a real difference. Our data is part of who we are, and we should guard it as carefully as we guard our wallets.

passages.title: Microplastics: A Hidden Problem
text: Microplastics are pieces of plastic smaller than five millimetres. Some are made small on purpose, such as the tiny beads once common in face scrubs, but most come from larger plastic items that break down over time under sunlight, wind, and waves. Synthetic clothes also release thousands of microscopic fibres every time they are washed.

Scientists have found microplastics almost everywhere they have looked: in deep oceans, on mountain tops, in drinking water, in sea salt, and in the bodies of fish and shellfish. Because these particles are so small, they are easily swallowed by marine animals and can move up the food chain to humans.

What this means for human health is not yet fully understood. Laboratory studies suggest that microplastics may cause inflammation in cells and may carry harmful chemicals that stick to their surfaces. However, most of these studies used much higher amounts of plastic than people are likely to consume, so researchers caution against drawing firm conclusions. Long-term studies on humans are still needed.

Even without complete answers, many scientists argue that it is sensible to reduce plastic pollution now rather than wait for proof of harm. Several countries have already banned microbeads in cosmetics, and some washing-machine makers are developing filters to catch fibres. Individuals can help too, for example by choosing natural fabrics and reducing their use of single-use plastics.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the text?

options.A: To persuade readers to buy electric motorbikes immediately
options.B: To criticize the government's subsidy policy
options.C: To explain how electric motors work
options.D: To present different views on switching to electric motorbikes

questions.explanation: Teks memaparkan argumen pendukung (paragraf 2) dan penentang (paragraf 3–4), lalu memberi simpulan seimbang. Inilah ciri discussion text.

questions.question:
Classify each point as an argument for or against switching to electric motorbikes.
(1) Maintenance is simpler and less frequent.
(2) Much electricity still comes from coal.
(3) Charging can take several hours.
questions.explanation: Perawatan yang sederhana adalah argumen pendukung. Listrik dari batu bara dan lamanya pengisian adalah keberatan dari pihak kritikus.

questions.question: The word Nevertheless in paragraph 4 signals that the next sentence ....

options.A: gives an example of the previous problem
options.B: introduces the conclusion of the whole text
options.D: presents a contrasting, more hopeful point

questions.explanation: Nevertheless adalah penanda pertentangan (= namun demikian). Setelah membahas masalah baterai, penulis menyebut solusi yang mulai muncul, yaitu stasiun tukar baterai.

questions.question: Which rider would the writer most likely advise to wait before buying an electric motorbike?

options.A: A student who rides five kilometres to school in Jakarta
options.B: An office worker who can charge at home and at the office
options.C: A delivery rider in a small town who travels 150 km a day
options.D: A shop owner who uses a motorbike only on weekends in the city

questions.explanation: Menerapkan simpulan: penulis menyarankan menunggu bagi pengendara yang jarak tempuhnya jauh atau tinggal di daerah dengan sedikit fasilitas pengisian. Jarak 150 km melebihi daya jelajah 60–100 km.

questions.question: What is the writer's position in the final paragraph?

options.A: Electric motorbikes are suitable for some riders but not yet for everyone.
options.B: Electric motorbikes should be banned until batteries improve.
options.C: Petrol motorbikes are always the better choice.
options.D: The government should stop building charging stations.

questions.explanation: On balance menandai simpulan yang menimbang kedua sisi: cocok untuk jarak pendek di kota dengan fasilitas memadai, sementara yang lain lebih baik menunggu.

questions.question: What is the writer's main claim?

options.A: Apps should not be allowed to collect any data.
options.B: Targeted advertising is the greatest danger online.
options.C: The 2022 law has solved the problem of data theft.
options.D: People should take their own data privacy seriously.

questions.explanation: Tesis di akhir paragraf 1: it is time we took our own data privacy seriously.

questions.question: Why does the writer mention Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law?

options.A: To acknowledge the role of laws before arguing they are not enough
options.B: To prove that individuals no longer need to be careful
options.C: To explain how to report a data leak
options.D: To criticize the government for acting too late

questions.explanation: Paragraf 4 diawali Admittedly (mengakui), lalu dibantah dengan However, laws cannot protect people who give their data away carelessly. Ini teknik konsesi lalu sanggahan.

questions.question: According to the text, how do many free apps earn money?

options.A: By charging users for extra features
options.D: By collecting users' data and selling it to advertisers

questions.explanation: Many free apps earn money by collecting information about users' habits and selling it to advertisers.

questions.question:
Which habits does the writer recommend?
(1) Checking app permissions before installing
(2) Using one strong password for all accounts
(3) Not sending identity card photos to unknown parties
(4) Avoiding all online forms
questions.explanation: Paragraf terakhir: membaca izin aplikasi, tidak mengirim foto dokumen identitas ke pihak tak dikenal, dan memakai kata sandi berbeda untuk setiap akun. Penulis tidak menyuruh menghindari semua formulir daring.

questions.question: The comparison in the final sentence (guard it as carefully as we guard our wallets) is used mainly to ....

options.A: show that data and money are stolen by the same criminals
options.B: explain how to store data in a safe place
options.C: make readers see personal data as something valuable that can be lost
options.D: suggest that people should carry less money

questions.explanation: Analogi dompet membuat pembaca memandang data pribadi sebagai harta berharga yang perlu dijaga. Ini strategi persuasi, bukan informasi teknis.

questions.question: According to the text, where do most microplastics come from?

options.B: Larger plastic items that break down

questions.explanation: most come from larger plastic items that break down over time. Butiran scrub hanyalah contoh microplastik yang sengaja dibuat kecil.

questions.question: Why do researchers caution against drawing firm conclusions about health effects?

options.A: Microplastics have never been found in humans.
options.B: Laboratory studies used larger amounts of plastic than people normally consume.
options.C: The particles are too small to study.
options.D: Most studies were done on fish, not cells.

questions.explanation: Paragraf 3: most of these studies used much higher amounts of plastic than people are likely to consume, sehingga hasilnya belum tentu berlaku bagi manusia.

questions.question: What is the writer's attitude towards the health risks of microplastics?

options.A: Certain that they are extremely dangerous
options.B: Careful and balanced, noting what is still unknown
options.C: Convinced that they are completely harmless

questions.explanation: Penulis memakai kata may, not yet fully understood, dan still needed. Sikapnya hati-hati dan berimbang.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes paragraph 4?

options.A: Scientists must prove that microplastics are harmful before anyone acts.
options.B: Reducing plastic pollution now is reasonable even though evidence is incomplete.
options.C: Washing machines are the main cause of microplastic pollution.
options.D: Natural fabrics are more expensive than synthetic ones.

questions.explanation: Kalimat utama paragraf 4: it is sensible to reduce plastic pollution now rather than wait for proof of harm, lalu diberi contoh tindakan negara, produsen, dan individu.

questions.question: The word synthetic in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ....
questions.explanation: Synthetic clothes = pakaian dari bahan buatan (misalnya poliester), lawan dari natural fabrics di paragraf 4.
